scenes.animation: Zippy stands at the foot of the Qutub Minar holding a very long measuring tape, trying to throw it to the top. The tape flops back onto his head.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: I need the height of this tower, but my tape won't go up!

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Keep your feet on the ground. One distance and one angle are enough.

scenes.animation: A student's eye at point P looks up at the top of the minar. A dotted green 'horizontal level' line runs from the eye; a red 'line of sight' runs from the eye to the top. The angle between them opens like a fan, labelled 'angle of elevation'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The line of sight is the line drawn from the eye of the observer to the point being viewed.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: When you look up at an object, the angle between the line of sight and the horizontal is the angle of elevation.

scenes.animation: Cut to a girl on a balcony looking down at a flower pot on the ground. The dotted horizontal line runs from her eye; the line of sight slopes down to the pot. The angle between them glows blue, labelled 'angle of depression'. Then a second horizontal at the pot appears and the equal alternate angle glows too.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: When you look down at an object, the angle between the line of sight and the horizontal is the angle of depression.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: So is it measured from the wall of the building?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: No. Always from the horizontal at the observer's eye. And since the two horizontals are parallel, the angle of depression from the balcony equals the angle of elevation from the pot.

scenes.animation: Worked example built step by step: vertical tower AB, point C on the ground, 'BC = 15 m', '∠ACB = 60°', right angle at B. Then: 'tan 60° = AB/BC', '√3 = AB/15', 'AB = 15√3 m'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Example: a tower stands vertically on the ground. From a point 15 metres from its foot, the angle of elevation of the top is 60 degrees. Find the height.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Draw tower AB and point C, with BC equal to 15 metres. Triangle ABC is right-angled at B.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: We know the adjacent side and want the opposite side, so we use tan. Tan 60 equals AB by BC.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Root three equals AB by 15, so AB is 15 root three metres.

scenes.animation: A 'BOARD TIP' card with a mini checklist: '1. Draw the figure', '2. Mark the right angle', '3. Mark the given angle from the horizontal', '4. Pick the ratio linking known and unknown sides'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Board tip: always draw a neat labelled figure first. The figure itself carries marks.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Then choose the ratio that links the side you know with the side you want. Known adjacent, unknown opposite? Use tan.

scenes.animation: Recap board with an eye icon looking up and down: '1. Elevation: looking up, from the horizontal', '2. Depression: looking down, from the horizontal', '3. Angle of depression = angle of elevation (alternate angles)'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Recap. One: the angle of elevation is measured up from the horizontal when you look up.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Two: the angle of depression is measured down from the horizontal when you look down.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Three: the angle of depression from above equals the angle of elevation from below, since they are alternate angles.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Tape retired. Protractor hired.

scenes.animation: Independence Day at school. A flag flutters on a flagstaff on top of a building. Zippy squints from the ground with a protractor: 'Building top: 30°. Flag top: 45°.'

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Two angles, one building, one flagstaff. My brain has two tabs open and both are loading.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Then we close one tab at a time. Two angles simply means two right triangles.

scenes.animation: A quick side example: a student of height 1.5 m stands 28.5 m from a chimney; angle of elevation 45°. Build: 'tan 45° = AE/DE', '1 = AE/28.5', 'AE = 28.5 m', 'Height = 28.5 + 1.5 = 30 m'. The '+1.5' flashes yellow.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: First, a common trap. A student 1.5 metres tall stands 28.5 metres from a chimney and sees its top at 45 degrees.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Tan 45 is one, so the part of the chimney above his eye level is 28.5 metres.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: But his eyes are 1.5 metres above the ground, so the chimney is 28.5 plus 1.5, which is 30 metres.

scenes.animation: Main figure drawn step by step: building AB = 10 m, flagstaff BD on top, point P on the ground. '∠APB = 30°' in orange, '∠DPA = 45°' in blue. Triangle PAB is shaded first.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Now the flag. From point P on the ground, the top of a 10 metre building is at 30 degrees, and the top of the flagstaff on it is at 45 degrees.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Find the length of the flagstaff and the distance of the building from P.

scenes.animation: Working written line by line beside triangle PAB: 'tan 30° = AB/AP', '1/√3 = 10/AP', 'AP = 10√3 m ≈ 17.32 m'. Then triangle PAD is shaded: 'tan 45° = AD/AP', '1 = (10 + x)/(10√3)', '10 + x = 10√3', 'x = 10(√3 − 1) = 10 × 0.732 = 7.32 m'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: In triangle PAB, tan 30 equals AB by AP. So one by root three equals 10 by AP, giving AP equals 10 root three, about 17.32 metres.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Let the flagstaff be x metres, so AD is 10 plus x. In triangle PAD, tan 45 equals AD by AP.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: One equals 10 plus x, over 10 root three. So 10 plus x equals 10 root three.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: x equals 10 into root three minus one, which is 10 into 0.732, that is 7.32 metres.

scenes.animation: A 'BOARD TIP' card: 'Find the common side first (here AP). Keep answers in surd form unless asked; use √3 = 1.732 only at the end.'

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: So the trick was finding AP first?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Exactly. Board tip: in two-triangle problems, find the side the triangles share first. Keep root three as it is until the last line, then use 1.732 if asked.

scenes.animation: Recap board with the flag icon: '1. Add the observer's height when the angle is measured from the eye', '2. Two angles → two right triangles sharing a side', '3. Keep surds till the end; √3 ≈ 1.732'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Recap. One: if the angle is measured from the observer's eye, add the observer's height at the end.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Two: two angles mean two right triangles, joined by a common side. Find it first.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Three: keep root three as a surd until the final step.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Both tabs loaded. Flag saluted!
